items.statement: Proactive personal contact by telephone or in person is associated with higher uptake of bereavement follow-up than a written invitation across palliative care services.
items.rationale: The retrieved evidence points this way (claims c1 and c3), and the answer decides whether the hospice keeps or expands its volunteer calls; novelty is low, which suits a rapid review that informs a local choice.
items.risks: Evidence is mostly before-after; publication bias toward positive service evaluations.

items.statement: Risk-screened targeting raises uptake among relatives at high risk without lowering uptake among others.
items.rationale: One regional network reported high uptake among relatives rated high risk, but outreach method changed at the same time.
items.risks: Few studies; screening completeness varies by time of death.

items.statement: Offering support at six weeks rather than two weeks increases uptake.
items.rationale: Colleagues disagree about timing, and one confounded comparison favoured six weeks.
items.risks: Likely too few comparable studies to answer.

summary: Three review-level hypotheses; h1 selected as the main question, with timing and risk targeting extracted as secondary questions.
